definitions.explanation: The practice of chanting the name of Amida Buddha, specifically the phrase 「{南無阿弥陀仏|なむあみだぶつ}」 (Namu Amida Butsu). Central to Pure Land Buddhism ({浄土宗|じょうどしゅう} and {浄土真宗|じょうどしんしゅう}), where it is believed to lead to rebirth in the Pure Land.

examples.japanese: {念仏|ねんぶつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{唱|とな}える→唱える：10467_tonaeru⟧。
⟦{祖母|そぼ}→祖母：00813_sobo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{毎朝|まいあさ}→毎朝：00966_maiasa⟧{念仏|ねんぶつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{唱|とな}えている→唱える：10467_tonaeru⟧。
examples.english: My grandmother chants the nenbutsu every morning.

examples.japanese: {法然|ほうねん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、{念仏|ねんぶつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{唱|とな}える→唱える：10467_tonaeru⟧こと⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{誰|だれ}→誰：00534_dare⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{救|すく}われる→救う：02063_sukuu⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{説|と}いた→説く：14245_toku⟧。
examples.english: Hōnen taught that anyone can be saved by chanting the nenbutsu.

notes:
USAGE:
The standard collocation is {念仏|ねんぶつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{唱|とな}える→唱える：10467_tonaeru⟧ (to chant the nenbutsu). The chant itself is 「{南無阿弥陀仏|なむあみだぶつ}」 (Namu Amida Butsu — "I take refuge in Amida Buddha").

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- ⟦{馬|うま}→馬：01865_uma⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{耳|みみ}→耳：01513_mimi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{念仏|ねんぶつ}: "nenbutsu in a horse's ear" — preaching to deaf ears, wasting one's breath

CULTURAL NOTE:
{念仏|ねんぶつ} is the core practice of {浄土宗|じょうどしゅう} (Jōdo-shū) and {浄土真宗|じょうどしんしゅう} (Jōdo Shinshū), which are among the most popular Buddhist traditions in Japan.
